report_name: TrueConf Installers Trojanized with Backdoors in Supply Chain Attack

threat_actors.name: Head Mare
threat_actors.description: A hacktivist group that conducted a supply chain attack against on-premise TrueConf video conferencing servers, replacing legitimate client installers with trojanized versions containing the PhantomCore and PhantomGraph backdoors.
threat_actors.goals: Distribute malware to users of compromised TrueConf servers to enable data theft and establish persistent access.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Head Mare exploited a chain of two vulnerabilities (KLCERT-26-057 and KLCERT-26-058) to escalate privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on the compromised TrueConf server.

attack_patterns.name: Server Software Component: Web Shell
attack_patterns.description: The attackers deployed a PHP web shell by replacing the legitimate file `\public\js\locale.php` to maintain persistent remote access and execute commands.

attack_patterns.name: Supply Chain Compromise
attack_patterns.description: Attackers compromised on-premise TrueConf servers and replaced legitimate client installers with trojanized versions, causing users to download and install backdoors.

attack_patterns.name: Web Service
attack_patterns.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor used a Microsoft OneDrive account for command and control communications.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
attack_patterns.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor was used to dump credentials from the LSASS process memory on compromised workstations.

malware.name: PhantomCore
malware.description: A primary backdoor payload delivered via trojanized TrueConf client installers. It likely provides remote access, command execution, and data exfiltration capabilities.

malware.name: PhantomGraph
malware.description: A secondary backdoor that uses a Microsoft OneDrive account for command and control and is capable of dumping LSASS memory to steal credentials.

vulnerabilities.name: KLCERT-26-057
vulnerabilities.description: The first of a two-vulnerability chain exploited by Head Mare to gain SYSTEM-level privileges on unpatched TrueConf servers.

vulnerabilities.name: KLCERT-26-058
vulnerabilities.description: The second of a two-vulnerability chain exploited by Head Mare to gain SYSTEM-level privileges on unpatched TrueConf servers.

infrastructure.name: PHP Web Shell Persistence
infrastructure.description: A PHP web shell was deployed by replacing `locale.php` on the TrueConf server to provide persistent access and execute commands.

infrastructure.name: PhantomGraph OneDrive C2
infrastructure.description: The PhantomGraph backdoor used a Microsoft OneDrive account as a C2 and exfiltration channel.

indicators.name: TrueConf Web Shell File Modification
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: TrueConf Web Shell File Modification
id: 2b1a9c8d-f3e4-4a1b-8c7d-6e5f4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects modification of the locale.php file on a TrueConf server, which is indicative of the Head Mare web shell deployment.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
level: high
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '\public\js\locale.php'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the modification of `locale.php` on TrueConf servers, a TTP used by Head Mare to deploy a web shell.

indicators.name: Anomalous Server Outbound to OneDrive
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Server Outbound Connection to OneDrive
id: 8d7c6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-1b9a-8c7d6e5f4d3c
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network connections from common server processes to Microsoft OneDrive, which may indicate C2 activity by malware like PhantomGraph.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1102
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'onedrive.live.com'
    Initiated: 'true'
  filter_client:
    Image|contains:
      - 'C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\'
      - 'C:\Users\'
  condition: selection and not filter_client
indicators.description: Detects anomalous outbound connections from a server to onedrive.live.com, a technique used by the PhantomGraph backdoor for C2.

indicators.name: LSASS Memory Dumping via Procdump
indicators.pattern:
title: LSASS Memory Dump via Procdump
id: 5a4b3c2d-1a9b-4c8d-f3e4-d2c1b9a8c7d6
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of procdump.exe to dump the LSASS process memory, a technique used for credential harvesting.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1003.001
level: critical
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\procdump.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '-ma'
      - 'lsass.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects command-line patterns for dumping LSASS memory using procdump, a technique associated with the PhantomGraph backdoor.

indicators.name: Suspicious Child Process from TrueConf Web Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Child Process from TrueConf Web Server
id: 1f9e8d7c-6b5a-4f3e-4d2c-1b9a8c7d6e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects a web server process, such as one used by TrueConf, spawning a command shell, which can indicate web shell execution.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/hackers-breach-trueconf-to-trojanize-client-installers-with-backdoors/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-09
tags:
  - attack.t1505.003
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects web server processes associated with TrueConf spawning command shells, a strong indicator of web shell activity.

relationships.source_name: Suspicious Child Process from TrueConf Web Server
